summary: Throughput degradation and intermittent request timeouts caused by GPU affinity + batch-size mismatch on dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Customer Streamlytic is experiencing sustained p95/p99 latency regressions and intermittent 504/timeout errors for inference requests on their dedicated us-west reservation. The pattern started after a week of burst traffic and a recent autoscaler tuning change.
impact: Multiple production routes for the customer saw p95 increase from ~120ms to 1.2s and p99 spikes to 3–6s. Approximately 12% of requests returned 504s during peak. This impacts the customer's real-time product and they've flagged this as a business-critical outage.
observed_behavior:
- Increased queue length on serving runtime during bursts
- GPU utilization near 100% on a subset of nodes while others show kernel idle time
- Frequent eviction/re-scheduling of worker pods due to perceived OOM/latency
- Autoscaler did not add capacity quickly enough; some new nodes remained underutilized with low batchable windows
- Prefix cache hit rate dropped during the event
expected_behavior: Stable p95/p99 latency within SLA, autoscaler scales smoothly to meet throughput, even distribution of load across GPUs with minimal evictions and consistent cache hit rates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a multi-route workload that sends 20 RPS of mixed short/long context requests to the customer's dedicated reservation.
2) Introduce synthetic burst: 300 concurrent short-context requests for 60s followed immediately by 50 concurrent long-context (>=4096 tokens) requests for 120s.
3) Observe serving runtime metrics (gpu_util, batch_size_distribution) and autoscaler decisions during and after burst.
4) Check request traces for head-of-line queuing and kernel start delays.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor - a small set of containers were pinning entire GPU resources due to long-context requests leading to head-of-line blocking for short requests.
Observed asymmetric GPU utilization: some GPUs at ~98% with long kernel runtimes, while others idle -> indicates affinity/packing issue at pod placement or batcher packing policy.
Autoscaler logs show scaling lag. The change deployed on 2026-02-28 reduced target batch window to lower latency but inadvertently reduced batch packing efficiency for mixed workloads.
Found scheduler affinity hinting disabled for this customer's pool, leading to interleaved placement of long-context and short-context pods on same GPUs, increasing kernel context switching.

Reproduction locally: identical burst reproduced increased p99 when batcher window set <10ms and packing policy disabled. Enabling packing policy forced long-context jobs to dedicated GPU slices and reduced p99.
Cross-referenced with telemetry: related PR github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2913 which modified the autoscaler trigger thresholds and batching defaults for low-latency tenants.
Opened INT-2210 to validate node-level GPU driver logs for thermal throttling — no clear thermal events, but there are frequent CUDA context switches logged.
actions_taken: 1) Temporarily applied placement constraint to favor colocating high-latency-only pods on separate nodes (hotfix) for Streamlytic's reservation (2026-03-10T16:10Z).
2) Increased autoscaler aggressive threshold to trigger earlier scale-up and added a short stabilisation window to avoid oscillation (2026-03-10T16:25Z).
3) Rolled back recent batch-window reduction for the affected pool and re-enabled packing policy override for mixed workloads (2026-03-10T17:05Z).
4) Notified customer and applied traffic shaping to reduce long-context concurrency while autoscale completes spin-up.
5) Collected additional traces and node-level GPU driver logs for deeper root cause analysis.

root_cause: Combination of (1) placement/pod-packing misconfiguration that allowed long-context/long-kernel pods to share GPUs with short-request pods causing head-of-line kernel contention, and (2) autoscaler tuning that reduced batch packing efficiency and delayed scale-up under mixed-burst traffic.
resolution: Applied placement constraint to separate long-context work, restored packing policy defaults, and adjusted autoscaler thresholds. Customer's p99 returned to acceptable range and 504 rate dropped to <1% within 45 minutes of fixes. Deliverables: recommend permanent scheduler affinity rules for dedicated pools running mixed workloads and a follow-up autoscaler configuration change staged via PR.
postmortem_next_steps: 1) Create PR to add packing-policy=true as default for dedicated pools serving mixed workloads (owner: infra).
2) Add an autoscaler guard that detects large long-context spikes and pre-emptively spins up capacity based on token-length histogram (owner: autoscale team).
3) Update runbook with steps to identify GPU packing issues and temporary mitigations (owner: SRE).
4) Schedule a customer brief with Streamlytic to explain changes and recommended constraints (owner: CS).
